title: Ngā Whetū o te Tau Hou | The Stars of the New Year
location: Te Whatu Stardome | Observatory & Planetarium, 670 Manukau Rd, Maungakiekie/One Tree Hill Domain, Epsom, Auckland 1023, Auckland
description:
In this immersive planetarium experience, you’ll journey through the night sky to explore the Matariki star cluster and its importance in Aotearoa and te ao Māori.
Discover the rich pūrākau (stories), science and traditions connected to each of the nine whetū, learn about the Maramataka (the Māori lunar calendar), and reflect on how Matariki guides us through the cycles of the year along with many other significant stars.
Whether you’re reconnecting with Matariki or experiencing it for the first time, this show is a great way to honour the season and gain a deeper appreciation of Māori astronomy and our place within the cosmos.
Keywords: Nga Whetu o te Tau Hou The Stars of the New Year

description:
**WHAT TO EXPECT**
Join us for another Hack The Box meetup in Auckland! Whether you're thinking about being a hacker or are already a seasoned one, this event has something for everyone.

The event will include a theory presentation and a guided walk through of an HTB challenge, demonstrating essential tools and techniques for enumeration and exploitation. At the end, we will do a raffle where we will give out HTB prizes, such as VIP access to the platform and HTB Academy cubes.

This is an on-site event in Auckland CBD.

**WHAT YOU GET**

* A chance to win some HTB giveaways
* Access to our HTB dedicated lab during the event

**WHAT YOU NEED**

* A laptop.
* A HTB account.
* Discord application.

**HOUSE RULES**

* Follow all rules and guidelines in the **[HTB TOS: HTB Terms of Service](https://www.hackthebox.com/tos)**
* Active HTB content cannot be shared publicly. Retired challenges or machines are fair game.
* CyberCX hosts the event to support the growth of the local cybersecurity community and to support students and professionals in their journeys to learn. Respect for the venue and people is expected from all the attendees.
* Note that sign-in will be required at the lobby (for security reasons only).

**ADDITIONAL NOTES**

* Join our Discord for event discussion, upcoming event announcements, and CTFs here: **[https://discord.gg/aDWymsDxWu](https://discord.gg/aDWymsDxWu)**
* Free parking is not available at the location.

**CODE OF CONDUCT**
We strive to create a safe, welcoming, and inclusive environment for all attendees. To ensure a positive experience for everyone, the following behaviors are strictly prohibited:

* Smoking
* Drinking alcohol
* Any form of discrimination or racism
* Any other forms of misconduct

Any attendee found engaging in these behaviours will be immediately banned and permanently removed from the group. Thank you for helping us maintain a respectful and enjoyable atmosphere for all.

title: Winter Light Cathedral
location: Aotea Square, 291-297 Queen Street, Auckland City Centre, Auckland, Auckland
description:
Wander through a glowing tunnel of light and feel the magic of winter come alive!
Step inside Winter Light Cathedral - a dazzling, walk-through experience made from tens of thousands of tiny LED lights. Inspired by the sweeping arches of grand church windows, this luminous tunnel invites you in for a moment of warmth, wonder and a little bit of WOW.
From the outside, it shines like a beacon in Aotea Square. Inside, it’s something else entirely - a sparkling, cosy world where every step surrounds you in soft, golden light.
Subtle by day and radiant after dark, whether you're out for a family night or date night this is a joyful experience not to miss.
Walk it once, snap a pic, tag us @aucklandlive, then go again - you’ll want to!
Hot tip: Visit on a Friday or Saturday night, between 6pm and 9pm, to watch neon-lit dancers bringing an extra touch of magic to the Cathedral. 
Free entry, just turn up and step into the magic. Open 24/7 (best to visit after dark).

title: Dinosaur Discovery Track experience
location: Auckland Zoo, 99 Motions Road, Western Springs, Auckland, Auckland
description:
A highly immersive educational experience of awe-inspiring creatures from the Cretaceous and Jurassic periods between 200 - 66 million years ago!
The track features 20 animatronic replicas of 15 different species that move and roar - created by world-leading dinosaur creators, The Dinosaur Company.
The Zoo’s 2026 experience highlights nature’s extraordinary terrestrial and marine giants - both past and present. Learn about the fascinating connections they have with species living at the Zoo and wildlife species the Zoo is helping conserve in the wild.
Among interactive activities are daily keeper talks with Dinosaur Rangers and the opportunity to try your hand as a palaeontologist by taking part in fossil digs.

title: Agentic AI Evaluation on Bedrock: Lessons from Pushpay's Journey
location: Level 19, Vero Centre, 48 Shortland Street, Auckland CBD, Auckland
description:
Hello everyone,

We're excited to invite you to the **Auckland AWS Tools and Programming meetup**!

This month, we are diving deep into the realities of moving AI from a cool demo to a production-ready system. We are thrilled to host two fantastic co-speakers: **[Roger Wang](https://www.linkedin.com/in/roger-nz/)** (Senior Solutions Architect @ AWS) and **[Saurabh Gupta](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nzsaurabh/)** (Pushpay).

We are gathering once again at the *Pushpay office in the CBD*—looking forward to seeing you all there!

🚨 **Action Required:** To help us streamline building security and sort out the catering (including dietary requirements), please make sure to pre-register before arriving: 👉 **[Pre-register for Venue Check-In Here](https://eventspaces.app/e/build-reliable-agentic-ai-solution-learn-from-pushpay-s-journey-on-agentic-ai-evaluation-f9b80e/register)**

⚠️ *Important Day Change: Please note that we are meeting on a Tuesday this month instead of our usual Thursday slot!*

**🎤 The Lineup**
**Roger Wang (AWS) & Saurabh Gupta (Pushpay)**

* **Title:** Breaking Through the 65% Ceiling: How Pushpay Engineered a 95% Accurate Production AI Agent
* **Description:** Agentic AI plateaus fast once you move beyond demos. Pushpay's natural language search agent hit a \~65% accuracy ceiling before the team built a structured evaluation framework to break through it.
Roger and Saurabh will walk through Pushpay's real-world journey: building the agent on **Amazon Bedrock**, why accuracy stalled, and the engineering techniques that pushed it to 95%. They will share practical takeaways including constructing a 300+ query golden dataset, automating measurement with LLM-as-a-Judge, and applying domain-specific prompt engineering on Bedrock. No hype—just real numbers, a real production system, and actionable insights for anyone building or operating agents.

title: Data & AI Management Meetup June 2026
description:
Join us for an insightful session exploring the future of the Data Governance practice in the AI age and how AI is transforming Data Quality management. Let’s share ideas, real stories, and novel ways to make your data work harder.

\*\*\*\*
5:30 pm - Welcome and Networking (drinks)

**Lisa Stewart** is the **Head of Data & AI Enablement and Governance** at Auckland Transport, where she leads enterprise strategy and delivery across data and AI governance, enablement, and capability uplift. When a five year old girl befriends a lonely migrant worker her family unravels; opening them up to face uncomfortable truths about themselves… and the world beyond their front gate.

title: Various artists: All the forest stands with you
location: Te Uru Waitākere Contemporary Gallery, 420 Titirangi Road, Titirangi, Auckland, Auckland
description:
all the forest stands with you traces the entangled relationalities between the human and the more-than-human world.
The exhibition brings together artists whose practices connect to a place where whenua, water, air and ancestral presence are not easily reduced to backdrop or resource, but remain active participants in shared worlds. Taking this condition not as an illustration, but as a proposition: to revisit, reevaluate and reimagine the status quo of our being in a world that is never solely human. 
Featuring artists:

Jonathas de Andrade
Anetta Mona Chişa
Ayesha Green
Arapeta Hākura
Emily Karaka

title: JuniorDev Auckland Meet
description:
We’re happy to announce the next **JuniorDev Auckland event**!

Join us for an evening of learning and connection as we hear from our speakers and the experiences they’ll be sharing.

**Important Note for Attendees:**

* **Please use the following link to pre-register for Xero Venue before arriving** [https://invites.envoy.com/group-invite/O8Ih4IdzCowjvyIM](https://invites.envoy.com/group-invite/O8Ih4IdzCowjvyIM).
* **The event venue entry will be closed at 6:30pm, please make sure you arrive on time.**

**Talk 1: From Zero Interviews to Real Projects: What to Build When No One's Calling Back? by Ismael Silva**
This talk is aimed squarely at where most of the room actually is right now — applying, waiting, wondering if the market has forgotten about them. The core idea is that waiting is the worst use of a junior's time, and there's a better way to spend those weeks that turns a CV into a portfolio and an interview into a conversation about something you've actually built.

The session will show that "building leverage" does not require massive side projects. It will also touch on the value of soft skills and leadership, making the discussion relevant for both junior and experienced developers.

**A bit about Ismael:**

* Ismael is a full-stack engineer specializing in Next.js, TypeScript, Node.js, and Postgres, and currently runs a small product studio called Base Logic Labs. Before transitioning into tech, he spent more than 20 years in public speaking, sales, and leadership roles, delivering over a thousand talks across various settings.

**Talk 2: How Fast Can You Rise? by Katrina Clokie**
Katrina meets a lot of ambitious young people who seem to believe that it's possible for them to advance in their careers at an aggressive pace (once they get their foot in the door).
